newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-STANKOWSKI WINS HAWAII TOURNAMET IN SUDDEN DEATH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STANKOWSKI WINS HAWAII TOURNAMET IN SUDDEN DEATH.

text.p: Paul Stankowski birdied the fourth hole of sudden death to win the $1.2 million United Hawaiian Open on Sunday.
Stankowski, Jim Furyk and Mike Reid all birdied the last hole of regulation to tie at 17 under par to force the play-off.
Reid, the overnight leader, shot a one under-par-71 at Waialae C.C. and then was eliminated on the first extra hole with a bogey.
Stankowski, who shot 70 in regulation, and Furyk, whose 68 equalled the low round of the day, each parred the first extra hole, then birdied the next two.
After a good chip on the par five 18th hole, Stankowski was able to tap-in for his second official PGA TOur win, and his fifth tournament title in the last 10 months.
Stankowski's win was worth $216,000 and broght him up to sixth place on the money list with $278,298. It also earned him 150 Ryder Cup points.
"I've never even thought about the Ryder Cup before now," said Stankowski. "If I can make it this year it would be a dream come true."
Said Stankowski, "I didn't hit the ball that great, but I made a ton of putts. I knew I had to stay patient. I stuck to my game play and came out on top again."
Though Stankowski, 27, just starting winning last April, he has followed every victory with another the next week.
Furyk, the defending champion who won this event in a three-hole play-off last year, was defeated this time by Stankowski's putter and his own.
Stankowski sank two big birdie putts in the play-off to keep it going, a 10 footer on the second extra hole and a 30 footer on the third.
On the back nine, Furyk was briefly two strokes ahead of both Stankowski and Reid, but took a disasterous four-putt on the 15th green for double bogey.

Said Furyk: "I feel that I lost the tournament several times today and won the tournament several times as well. I'm very disappointed, but I know that no one played better than me today. Paul probably played as well, and one of us had to be disappointed."
